utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-13/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mile Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mrksic, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Please be seated. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. For Prosecution side, my name is Jan Wubben, Senior Trial Attorney. At my side, Mr. Mark McKeon, attorney, and Ms. Diane Boles, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. The Defence will be represented today by attorney Miroslav Vasic, Defence counsel for the accused Mile Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, too. So welcome to this Status Conference which is being convened according to Rule, or pursuant to Rule 65 bis, which requires us to hold a Status Conference more or less every four months, within 120 days from the previous one. The previous one was held on the 11th of November, as you may recall, so we are within the time limit. The purpose of such status conferences, I may summarise very shortly, is to give an opportunity for exchanges to be made between the parties with a view to ensuring an expeditious preparation for the trial, and in addition, to give an opportunity to the accused himself present here in the courtroom to raise any issue that he might think appropriate in relation to his condition of detention as well as his health condition, both physical and mental. In preparation for this Status Conference, I had given instructions to the senior legal officer, Mr. Von Hebel, to hold a 65 ter (D) conference, inviting you both to attend, and I am informed that this was held a few days ago, on the 3rd of March, and that in the course of this 65 ter meeting, you registered agreement on various issues that were raised and that some of them, I am informed, need not be discussed at any depth in this Status Conference. However, I will be referring to them just to confirm that there is nothing, no afterthoughts on the part of either of you and that you still stand by this position. I will deal with the various items on this agenda seriatim as they appear on the agenda for the status conference itself, and the first of these issues, of course, is outstanding motions that there are. The most important outstanding motion is the one containing pleadings on the part of the Defence on the form of the indictment. This has engaged -- I am told that this need not actually be discussed at any length or at any depth in the course of this Status Conference. This Defence pleading is of such importance that it has naturally engaged my legal staff considerably and with the result that, in order to be able to hand down an appropriate and comprehensive, full decision, we require a little bit more time. It is anticipated, however, and I know that you have been informed accordingly during the 65 ter meeting, that while I assure you that the matter is receiving our utmost attention, that we anticipate that we should be in a position to hand down a decision towards the end of this current month. Then there is another outstanding issue which is of much lesser importance, and that is the Defence motion for review of the Registrar's decision of the 25th of September, 2002, denying payment of expenses related to pre-trial investigative work. We have gone into this matter as far as it required our immediate attention at the time it was presented. If we are satisfied at any time between now and the commencement of the trial that the Registrar's decision, if implemented - because it has not been implemented - if implemented will seriously hamper your efforts in the preparation of the trial, then obviously we will intervene within the Rules and also in the light of the recent decision handed down by the Appeals Chamber in another case, which deals with the Registrar's discretion and mode of exercising its discretion in such and similar matters. I would suggest that you go to this judgement unless you have already perused it, because it may be important. In any case, it is my suggestion to you that we can sleep over this matter for the time being and that it will receive attention and priority as it deserves if and when it deserves such priority. Okay? Can you live with that, Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And the next item on the agenda is disclosure matters or issues. More or less I am informed that this was thrashed out to everyone's satisfaction during this 65 ter meeting, but I will just go through the various points one by one to make sure that the information that I have is not only correct -- I mean, I never doubt the correctness of the information that I received, but from experience, I know that sometimes after the meeting has been concluded one has afterthoughts, remembers, or figures out other things as well and there may be fresh matters that you would like to raise. Let's take them one by one. As far as 66(A)(i) material is concerned, I understand there is agreement amongst you that this exercise has been completed and that we need not discuss it any further. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: With regard to Rule 66(A)(ii), again I am told that you agreed during the last Status Conference and also during the last 65 ter meeting with my senior legal officer that you would commence this disclosure process or exercise once preliminary motions have been disposed of. Do I take it that you stand by this agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We will do that as soon as practical.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the Defence is concerned, we believe that the agreement reached with my learned friend will start to function as soon as we receive decisions regarding the preliminary objections and motions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And then there is the matter of reciprocal disclosure, and I'm not surprised to find in the report that Mr. Vasic pointed out that, in his opinion, it's still too early to say whether the Defence will trigger reciprocal disclosure at this point. So I take it that we will visit this matter at some subsequent point in time when one would expect a different kind or a more definitive mode of approach on the part of the Defence. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the last matter relating to disclosure and that envisaged under Rule 68 relating to exculpatory material. I am informed by my senior legal officer that the Prosecution indicated that it had devised a plan which it was proposing to the Defence -- to the Defence, showing how it intended or it planned to discharge its obligation to disclose exculpatory material. I am told that when this came up during the 65 ter meeting, you had practically just been provided with a copy or in any case that you had not had time or the opportunity to go through the relative document. May I ask your view, if you have reviewed it now and whether you have any comments to make, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have asked for some time to study the document, and I've done so, and I met with my learned friend the next day, the representative of the Prosecution, and I had no objections to raise regarding the method envisaged by the Prosecution to submit to the Defence documents pursuant to Rule 68. From the memorandum signed by me, it can be seen that the beginning of the disclosure under Rule 68 would begin at the end of March, which is acceptable. And we have agreed regarding the method of search and possible updating of the key criteria for searching through all the files in the possession of the Prosecution. The Defence has also asked the Prosecution to be kind enough, as that is their duty under this Rule, in addition to these criteria, to take certain steps to find any exculpatory material for the accused. So the Defence counsel has signed this document, and we agree with the proposed method of disclosure pursuant to Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Vasic. Just for the record, it is being pointed out by me that I have now been handed a document which substantially is the Rule 68 disclosure plan to which reference has been just made and that the relative document is signed by Mr. Vasic on behalf of the accused Mr. Mrksic, indicating his agreement to the plan itself. The Pre-Trial Judge orders that this document will be entered into the records of the case and will form an integral part thereof. Thank you. Before I close the matter, the item on the agenda dealing with disclosure, is there anything else either of you would like to raise in this regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Nothing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We come to the next item, which is the date of trial. I know that this was touched upon, dealt with in the course of the 65 ter meeting. The only thing that I would like to say is that I -- it is my opinion that the general assessment that was made and that you were informed about in the course of 65 ter meeting is also what I believe will be the case. It's not likely at all that this case could start this year or by early next year. However, it is one of the cases that is receiving attention by the Tribunal, and we will do our utmost to bring it to trial at the earliest possible opportunity. In the meantime, it may not be futile on my part to remind you that there is always the possibility that, pending the commencement of the trial and the determination of preliminary issues, you might find it useful or beneficial, particularly on your part, Mr. Vasic, and on the part of your client, to discuss or negotiate with the Prosecution any possible arrangements or plea bargaining that you may or may not wish to enter into. It's entirely up to you. The Trial Chamber is just mentioning this in case your client thinks that there is absolutely no way out but to wait until the trial comes, the trial date arrives and that a full trial has to take place on the basis of what he has been charged with and nothing else. Perhaps you would like at some point in time to discuss this with your client, and I'm pretty sure that the Prosecution would be open to discuss any suggestions that you might have in this context. You need not comment on what I said, because as I said, it's entirely up to you. Having said this, I come to one of the items that I consider very important in every Status Conference, and I'm going to address you directly, Mr. Mrksic. I want to know if you have any reason to complain about the condition of your detention here in The Hague at the detention centre.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no complaints to make. The personnel in the Detention Unit are very correct in their dealings with us, as is the administration, and I think they can set an example as far as that is concerned. As far as my health is concerned, you know that I had two heart surgeries, and life in the Detention Unit, the healthy way of life, daily exercise, have in fact contributed to an improvement of my heart condition. It's been 15 months since the surgery, and I would like to have an examination with specialists, if possible, so as to avoid any surprises. In the meantime, I had some problems with my prostate gland. The elderly will understand what those problems entail. I have been given medicines to take for a month and a half. Afterwards, there will be some screening of my bladder. I don't really know what is involved. So that is the only health problem that I have and no others at all. I would just like to point out that we are being very correctly treated, both here at the Tribunal and in the Detention Unit. I hope that the cooperation between the Defence and the Prosecution will be fruitful, that certain truths will be discovered to our common satisfaction. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Mrksic. Having heard what you had to say in regard to your state of health and concerns that you have thereon, the Pre-Trial Chamber orders that the relevant parts of the transcript, that is the entire statement of Mr. Mrksic, be communicated to the commandant of the Detention Unit, Mr. McFadden, for his information, attention -- for his attention and any action that he may deem appropriate after consultation with the necessary medical personnel that he deems fit to consult. I am communicating to Mr. McFadden your statement, which is in itself an invitation to him to -- first I'm making him aware that you have got these concerns about your health; and secondly, I'm telling him make an assessment together with the medical experts that you have available and see what this gentleman needs by way of medical treatment. And I can assure you that you will receive all the necessary medical treatment that you require. However, I do want to make it clear that if you are not happy with the way your medical -- your health is being attended to, please feel free to let me know. Please feel free to communicate any complaints or any concerns that you may have to your lawyer, and your lawyer knows exactly how to reach me in order to communicate those complaints to me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have absolutely no complaints to make regarding medical personnel. It's simply a question of age, and I am sure that the problems will be resolved with the help of medical experts. And I hope after these medicines and tests, the worst will not happen, but one reaches an age when one can only expect problems of this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what interpretation you received, but at no time did I read what you said as meaning that you were complaining against any of the medical personnel. What I understood is that you had concerns about the needs by way of medical attention that you may think you require. You may require them, you may not require them; these matters are usually decided by doctors themselves. But anyway, the entire transcript of this phase, this part of the proceedings, will be communicated to Mr. McFadden, who, I can assure you, I can guarantee to you, will give this matter his utmost attention. He is the most responsible person that you can imagine, and he will give this matter his utmost attention. So having said that, may I ask either of you if you have got any other matter that you would like to raise before we adjourn?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence also has no questions to raise really, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Vasic. So the status conference stands adjourned and I will convene the next one towards the end of June, beginning of July, unless, of course, there is an urgent reason to convene another one in between. Thank you.
